note: No psoriasis model was ever run: the three JAK1-selective inhibitors went into psoriasis patients on a human whole-blood selectivity assay and rat arthritis, all three cleared plaques in Phase 2, none went further, and the JAK2-sparing premise of the selectivity assay was contradicted by dose-related platelet and reticulocyte falls.
label: Psoriasis (JAK1)

engagement.model: Human whole-blood cytokine-induced STAT phosphorylation (JAK1 potency and selectivity assay)
engagement.note: Abrocitinib was optimised from tofacitinib on nanomolar potency and JAK1 selectivity in a human whole-blood STAT-phosphorylation assay before any patient was dosed.
engagement.short: Whole-blood STAT assay set JAK1 selectivity
engagement.quote: Through modification of the 3-aminopiperidine linker in tofacitinib, we discovered highly selective JAK1 inhibitors with nanomolar potency in a human whole blood assay.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Year is a proxy: the assay predates the first-in-human study NCT01835197 (started 2013-05); the paper itself was published 2018-01-23.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at model_first_use_year by proxy (Phase 1 start 2013-05) rather than the 2018 publication date, as the brief allows. The FDA review of abrocitinib (atopic dermatitis) filed the same in-vitro cell-system STAT-phosphorylation data, so model_filed is true. Itacitinib used the same kind of assay in primary human lymphocytes (Covington 2020, doi 10.1016/j.ejphar.2020.173505), published after its psoriasis trial.

engagement.model: Human whole-blood cytokine-induced STAT phosphorylation (JAK1 potency and selectivity assay)
engagement.note: First-in-human dose escalation of abrocitinib (3-800 mg) in 79 healthy volunteers: pharmacodynamic biomarkers moved as JAK-signalling inhibition predicts.
engagement.short: JAK PD biomarkers moved in volunteers
engagement.quote: Changes in pharmacodynamic biomarkers were consistent with the known effects of Janus kinase signalling inhibition.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only: the abstract does not name the biomarkers, so whether the readout was ex-vivo STAT phosphorylation (direct) or a downstream haematology marker could not be verified; the Europe PMC full text returned a server error. Scored at the conservative downstream tier.
engagement.reason: JAK PD biomarkers moved in volunteers
engagement.judgement: Called same on direction only: the model's readout is cytokine-induced STAT phosphorylation in human blood and the Phase 1 reports JAK-inhibition-consistent biomarker changes at the doses later used in psoriasis (200-400 mg). Healthy volunteers count under the brief. NCT01835197 has no results posted, so registry_date is null. Solcitinib's psoriasis study (Ludbrook 2016, doi 10.1111/bjd.14399) also showed inflammatory gene-expression change in lesional skin after 2 weeks, a downstream readout in patients, but no public solcitinib model paper exists to pair it with.

dose.model: Rat (6-month) and cynomolgus monkey (39-week) repeat-dose toxicology
dose.note: Pivotal rat and monkey repeat-dose studies showed only the expected lymphocyte decrease; the monkey NOAEL was the top dose, 75 mg/kg/day.
dose.short: Rat and monkey tox: lymphocytes only
dose.quote: In a pivotal 39-week oral repeat dose toxicity study in monkeys, abrocitinib (doses: 0, 15, 35, and 75 mg/kg/day) decreased lymphocytes at all dose levels consistent with its intended pharmacological effect, but had no adverse effects.
dose.judgement: Year is a proxy: IND 123554 opened 2014-10-30 with the psoriasis Phase 2 as the 30-day safety study, so the toxicology package existed by then; the review itself was posted with the 2022 atopic-dermatitis approval. This is the only member with a public toxicology package: itacitinib and solcitinib never reached an NDA.

dose.model: Rat (6-month) and cynomolgus monkey (39-week) repeat-dose toxicology
dose.note: The monkey NOAEL (AUC 55,200 ng·h/mL) sits several-fold above the 200 mg clinical exposure; psoriasis patients took 200-400 mg/day for 4 weeks and were dosed to effect without the model's lymphocyte harm limiting them.
dose.short: Monkey NOAEL margin held in patients
dose.quote: The NOAEL was 75 mg/kg/day, which corresponds to Day 273 AUC24 and Cmax of 55200 ng·hr/mL and 5170 ng/mL, respectively.
dose.confidence_note: The margin is a toxicology NOAEL checked against clinical exposure, not an efficacy exposure target: no public source compares the rat-arthritis effective exposure with patient PK. The exposure multiples in the review and label are stated for the atopic-dermatitis dose, hence imported_from.
dose.reason: Monkey NOAEL margin held in patients
dose.judgement: Scored under decision 16 as a stated tolerability margin that held: the model's stated harm (lymphocyte decrease) did not stop dosing to target at 200 mg in atopic dermatitis or at 200-400 mg/day in psoriasis (Schmieder 2018, doi 10.1111/bjd.16004, 'well tolerated'). The harm the model did not state (platelet decrease) is counted once, in safety, as the brief directs. A stricter reading keeps dose untested because no efficacy exposure target was ever published for any member.
dose.magnitude_basis: AUC24 at NOAEL vs clinical AUC

efficacy.model: Rat adjuvant-induced arthritis (cross-indication; no psoriasis model was run)
efficacy.note: Abrocitinib was nominated on rat adjuvant arthritis for 'JAK1-mediated autoimmune diseases'; itacitinib likewise on rodent arthritis and colitis. No member was tested in a psoriasis model.
efficacy.short: Rat arthritis, not psoriasis, picked the candidate
efficacy.quote: After demonstrating efficacy in a rat adjuvant-induced arthritis (rAIA) model, PF-04965842 (25) was nominated as a clinical candidate for the treatment of JAK1-mediated autoimmune diseases.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Year is a proxy for the candidate nomination before the 2013 Phase 1; the paper was published 2018-01-23.
efficacy.judgement: The FDA review of abrocitinib lists no in-vivo pharmacology study, only in-vitro JAK selectivity and cell-system STAT phosphorylation, so model_filed is false. Covington 2020 (doi 10.1016/j.ejphar.2020.173505) is the itacitinib counterpart (rodent arthritis, three mouse colitis models, GvHD), published after the psoriasis trial. Nothing preclinical is public for solcitinib.

efficacy.model: Rat adjuvant-induced arthritis (cross-indication; no psoriasis model was run)
efficacy.note: All three members hit their Phase 2 primary endpoint in plaque psoriasis (abrocitinib PASI at week 4, itacitinib sPGA at day 28, solcitinib PASI 75 at week 12); none was taken further in psoriasis.
efficacy.short: Class cleared plaques as rat arthritis implied
efficacy.quote: At week 4, the proportion of patients achieving PASI 75 was 17% for the placebo and 200 mg OD groups, 50% for the 400 mg OD group and 60% for the 200 mg TD group.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for all three trials. The model is an arthritis model, so the agreement is with the class premise (JAK1 inhibition treats autoimmune inflammation), not with a psoriasis-specific prediction; a stricter reading leaves this cell an empty list because no psoriasis model was relied on.
efficacy.reason: Class cleared plaques as rat arthritis implied
efficacy.judgement: Called same, direction only, as a paired comparison (model paper January 2018, trial paper March 2018; the trial's registry results had posted 2016-10-05 and the itacitinib and solcitinib trials were already published in 2016). The abrocitinib trial was stopped at 59 of 196 planned patients on 2015-06-25 'due to changes in the sponsor's development priorities', not for efficacy; Pfizer took the drug to atopic dermatitis, Incyte took itacitinib to GvHD, and GSK stopped solcitinib after DRESS and liver-enzyme rises in lupus (Kahl 2016, doi 10.1177/0961203316640910). furthest_phase 2: no Phase 3 was ever run in psoriasis, so outcome_tested is null.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of PASI change vs placebo

patient_trials.quote: The estimated treatment effect (active -placebo PASI change from baseline) and 90% confidence interval at week 4 was -5·1 (-9·2 to -1·0), -5·6 (-9·6 to -1·6) and -10·0 (-14·2 to -5·8) for the 200 mg OD, 400 mg OD and 200 mg TD groups, respectively.
INCB039110 produced significant improvements in sPGA, demonstrating proof of concept in chronic plaque psoriasis.

At week 12, a 75% reduction in PASI (PASI 75) response rates in the intent-to-treat population were 0% in the placebo group compared with 13%, 25% and 57% in the 100 mg, 200 mg and 400 mg GSK2586184 twice-daily groups, respectively.

safety.model: Human whole-blood cytokine-induced STAT phosphorylation (JAK1 potency and selectivity assay)
safety.note: The selectivity assay's stated promise: inhibit JAK1-paired cytokines while sparing the JAK2 homodimer that carries erythropoietin and thrombopoietin signalling.
safety.quote: As JAK1 pairs with JAK2, JAK3, and TYK2, a JAK1-selective inhibitor would be expected to inhibit many cytokines involved in inflammation and immune function while avoiding inhibition of the JAK2 homodimer regulating erythropoietin and thrombopoietin signaling.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Year is a proxy for the assay's use before the 2013 Phase 1; the paper was published 2018-01-23.
safety.judgement: This is the model's explicit safety prediction, so the track can be scored on it rather than on silence.

safety.model: Rat (6-month) and cynomolgus monkey (39-week) repeat-dose toxicology
safety.note: Rat and monkey repeat-dose studies recorded lymphocyte decreases and rat urinary crystals; the review's nonclinical sections record no platelet effect in either species.
safety.quote: In a pivotal 6-month oral repeat dose toxicity study in rats, abrocitinib (doses: 0, 30, 45, and 70 mg/kg/day) decreased lymphocytes at all dose levels consistent with its intended pharmacological effect.
safety.confidence_note: Year is a proxy for the IND (opened 2014-10-30); the review was posted with the 2022 approval.
safety.judgement: Opening entry for the toxicology track in safety; silence on platelets was established by searching the review's nonclinical sections, not from a reviewer statement.

safety.model: Human whole-blood cytokine-induced STAT phosphorylation (JAK1 potency and selectivity assay)
safety.note: Psoriasis patients on 200 mg twice daily showed low neutrophil, reticulocyte and platelet counts, the JAK2-type haematology the selectivity assay said the drug would spare.
safety.short: Platelets and reticulocytes fell despite JAK2 sparing
safety.quote: There were more abnormal laboratory test results of clinical interest (low neutrophil, reticulocyte and platelet counts) in the 200 mg TD group compared with the OD treatment groups.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the abstract gives no counts or incidence, so the size of the miss is not computed.
safety.judgement: Contra because the model made an explicit prediction (sparing of JAK2-dependent erythropoietin and thrombopoietin signalling) that psoriasis patients contradicted within 4 weeks; the harm was in-context, not imported. magnitude is set to opposite because the prediction was absence of the harm. The FDA review later confirmed a dose-related platelet fall across the programme with a 0.2% rate of confirmed counts below 50,000/mm3 at 200 mg. Solcitinib's DRESS and liver-enzyme rises in lupus (van Vollenhoven 2015, doi 10.1177/0961203315573347; Kahl 2016) are the class's other harm, but no solcitinib model is public to score them against, so they are recorded here only.
safety.magnitude_basis: predicted sparing of JAK2-dependent thrombopoietin and erythropoietin signalling vs observed platelet and reticulocyte decreases

safety.model: Rat (6-month) and cynomolgus monkey (39-week) repeat-dose toxicology
safety.note: FDA: continuous abrocitinib gave a dose-related platelet decrease (nadir by 4 weeks, partial recovery on treatment), modelled on data that include the psoriasis Phase 2; rat and monkey tox had recorded none.
safety.short: Dose-related platelet fall the animals missed
safety.quote: Continuous administration of abrocitinib resulted in a dose-related decrease in platelet count.
safety.confidence_note: Silence of the animal studies inferred from the review's nonclinical sections (no platelet or thrombocytopenia mention in rat or monkey), not from a reviewer statement that the species missed it. The clinical statement is from the atopic-dermatitis programme, but the review's platelet model pools the psoriasis Phase 2 B7451005 with the AD studies.
safety.reason: Rat and monkey tox missed platelet fall
safety.judgement: Scored contra as silence contradicted on a harm both species could have shown (thrombocytopenia is a standard repeat-dose readout). imported_from is set because the quoted clinical finding is the pooled AD-led analysis; the same harm appears in psoriasis patients in Schmieder 2018. Counted here, not in dose, because the model did not predict it (decision 16).
